pairs.difference: A: the telescope is drawn small and whole in the middle of a wide moon floor. A high horizon line sits behind it with craters running back into the distance, so the object is a figure standing in a landscape. Planar share is 0.011, almost no flat faces. B: the camera is close and high over the binoculars. The barrels converge gently, the lens ends overlap the frame edge and the floorboards recede at one angle. This matches the tight, turned framing of the real camera card.
pairs.fix: Move the camera close and slightly above, turned three-quarters to the telescope. Let the tube fill the card and run off one edge. Show only a strip of ground under the tripod feet, with no far horizon or distant craters.

pairs.difference: A: the moon dome is a small object set back on a large gray plain, with a high horizon and a crater in the far background. The camera looks down from far away, so there are three separate depth bands. B: the camera is close at the bar counter. The thatch roof and the stools are cut by the frame edges, and the pool floor reads at one steady angle. The real cards use this close crop.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera in so the dome and airlock tube fill the card and touch the edges. Keep a low three-quarter view with a little ground showing, and remove the distant plain and horizon.

pairs.difference: A: the rover is shown almost side-on, centered and fully contained, on a cratered ground that runs back to a horizon. Its top face is barely visible, and the wheels stack flat with little foreshortening. B: the taxi is turned three-quarters with mild convergence, and the road stripes recede at one angle under the wheels. This matches the turned real vehicle cards (camper, bike).
pairs.fix: Turn the rover three-quarters toward the viewer from slightly above, so the front wheels look larger than the back ones. Crop close, so the ground is a simple floor under the wheels and there is no distant horizon.

pairs.difference: A: the control box is seen from high up. A large top face with dials and buttons faces the camera, and the box sits on a riveted metal floor whose tile lines converge somewhat strongly toward the back. B: the popcorn cart is at eye level, turned slightly, on paving that lies flat, with a plain backdrop. Both are plausible. A's raised camera and more pronounced floor convergence lean generated.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to about the height of the panel's top edge and turn the box a little. Show less of the top face and keep the floor tiles nearly parallel.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is a frontal, symmetric view with no ground, the same as the real flat-on clock card. B: the asteroid floats with no ground plane and is turned so the craters face the viewer, but its flame tails point off at an angle the rock body doesn't share. Its normals are smooth, swollen gradients with a planar share of 0.26. The view is weakly inconsistent. There is little viewpoint evidence either way.
pairs.fix: Show the asteroid from one clear three-quarter angle, with the flame trail streaming straight back from it in the same direction the rock is moving.

pairs.difference: A: the flip-flops are seen from high above, the pair is set on one diagonal, and the soles foreshorten together. B: Saturn's ring is tilted as an ellipse, but the band around the sphere and the porthole sit at a slightly different tilt from the ring. Both float with no ground. B's mismatched tilts lean generated.
pairs.fix: Tilt the ring and the bands around the planet to exactly the same angle, as if both are seen from one camera slightly above.

pairs.difference: A: the flowerbed is seen from moderately high, with the stone ring as an even ellipse on a flat floor. B: the folding chair is turned three-quarters at eye level on a curved floor that meets the backdrop. Both use mild perspective and one consistent ground, and neither breaks the viewpoint pattern of the real cards.

A: the helmet sits on a tabletop slab whose front edge cuts diagonally across the lower left. The camera is very close and near frontal on the visor, while the table plane recedes at a steeper angle than the stand's ellipse. B: the sneakers are low and turned, on a floor that meets a flat backdrop at one horizon, like the real barrel and camera cards.
pairs.fix: Make the table top and the round base share one camera height: a slightly raised three-quarter view in which the base's ellipse matches the angle of the table edge. Turn the helmet a little so the visor is not straight-on.

pairs.difference: A: the satellite dish is centered and fully contained on a square slab, in a wide desert that runs back to distant mesas on a low horizon. The scattered rocks and grass at several depths make a deep landscape, and the object is small in the frame. B: the sandcastle fills the card, and the bucket and shovel overlap it in the foreground with the sea simplified behind. This is the close, layered framing of the real cards.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera close so the dish and its base fill the card, and drop the distant mesas. Show only sand right around the base, with a simple sky behind.

pairs.difference: A: the UFO disc is seen from slightly above. Its top is one large even patch on the normal map (planar share 0.541), and the dome on top looks nearly side-on while the rim ellipse is open, so the parts don't quite agree on one view. B: the music player is turned at a steep three-quarter angle, and the earbuds and cable fall in front with consistent overlap.
pairs.fix: Draw the saucer from one camera slightly above, with the glass dome tilted toward the viewer at the same angle as the rim, so its base shows as an ellipse matching the disc.

pairs.difference: A: the submarine is a gentle three-quarter side view with the propeller receding, all at one angle. B: the rocket floats on a diagonal, but its two fins splay as if seen from a different, more frontal angle than the round body. The flame and nozzle read as almost side-on. There is no ground in either card.
pairs.fix: Turn the rocket so the fins and body share one view: one fin pointing toward the viewer and the others foreshortened around the round body, tilted on the diagonal.

pairs.difference: A: the camera is very low, down at the golf ball on the grass. The club runs off the top edge and the hills sit behind as simpler layers, like the real bike-rack card. B: the umbrella floats tilted, with the canopy and pole agreeing on one view. Neither breaks the viewpoint pattern of the real cards.

pattern: The generated cards pull the camera back. The object is centered, small and fully contained in a wide scene with a distant horizon, deep ground, scattered rocks and craters, or far mesas. Real cards crop close, turn the object three-quarters, and let it touch or run off the frame edge, with only a short strip of simple ground. Weaker signs are parts that don't share one tilt (a ring against bands, fins against body, a dome against its rim) and ground planes that recede more steeply than the object's own ellipses.
